versions.statuteQuote: The landlord may not charge any liquidated damages.

summaryForModel: When a victim of family abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, or trafficking ends a lease early under § 55.1-1236, the landlord may not charge liquidated damages, such as a lease-break or early termination fee. A lease that charges one in that case conflicts with this.
paraphraseExamples: All early terminations, for any reason, are subject to a termination fee of two months' rent.
Tenant who vacates before the end of the term forfeits the deposit as liquidated damages, without exception.
tenantExplanation: If you end your lease early because of abuse, stalking, or trafficking, your landlord can't charge you a lease-break fee.
action: You can ask your landlord to state that the lease-break fee does not apply in this case.
